fields.h1: Build a Library Survey Your Patrons Finish
fields.hero_description: Build a library survey patrons answer on any phone, with every response saved to a database your library owns.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Library Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe your patrons and the decision ahead, and Emergent builds the survey they answer and the table that holds every response.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your patrons

Tell Emergent who uses the library and what the board has to decide, such as weekend hours. Emergent drafts questions to fit, and a follow-up prompt rewords or cuts any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Answers kept apart from names

Ask for an anonymous survey, and each answer is saved with no name or card number beside it. Staff read the totals and every comment without knowing which patron wrote which one.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Patrons scan a QR code at a table or tap the link in an email, then answer one question per screen. Emergent sets no cap on responses, so a busy branch never closes the survey early.
fields.feature_4:
Every response in a database you own

Each response is a row in a database the library owns, tagged with the branch and the date. Put this year's answers beside last year's when the board reviews hours or study space.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts when a score drops

Pick a question and a threshold, such as a quiet rating below 3 out of 5. When the average falls under it, the app emails the branch manager the score and a link to the comments.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Run the survey on the library's own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it next year.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Library Surveys and What Changed
fields.tab_content_1:
Sunday hours, which 263 cardholders asked for

Fenwick Falls Public Library has always closed on Sundays, and the board wanted to know if it should. The library emailed its 2,400 cardholders a survey listing four time slots when the doors are shut. Of the 612 who answered, 263 picked Sunday afternoon. Starting in March, the library opens on Sundays, 1 to 5 pm.
fields.tab_content_2:
Second floor goes silent before finals after a 2.4 for quiet

Dellmont College library runs short of quiet seats in exam weeks. A QR code on each study table opens a 3-question survey that rates the quiet on that floor out of 5. A floor averaging below 3 emails the library dean. The second floor averaged 2.4 across 418 ratings and became a silent floor for finals week.
fields.tab_content_3:
Graphic novels or fantasy? Novels win with 141 votes

Each semester, the Tamsin Hill Middle School librarian asks students what they want on the shelves. They open the link on a phone or school laptop, and no names are saved. This spring 296 answered: 141 for graphic novels, 82 for fantasy. Of the $1,200 spring book order, $600 went to graphic novels.
fields.tab_content_4:
Laptop lending makes it into the 2027 plan

Orrin County Library wanted residents who never come in to shape its 2027 strategic plan. Links went up at all 5 branches and in the county newsletter, and 1,140 residents answered, each tagged by branch. At Eastgate, 88 of 210 asked for laptops to borrow, and the board wrote laptop lending into the plan.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Library Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a library survey that reaches more than the regulars and ends in one decision, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the decision the survey feeds
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Reach people who never come in
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what the board will decide, such as Sunday hours or the spring book order, before you draft a single question. Cut every question that cannot move that decision. Put the decision in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A paper survey at the circulation desk only hears from regulars. Email the link to every cardholder and print a QR code for the community center bulletin board, so residents who have never borrowed a book can answer too.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask which hours a patron would use, not whether the library should open longer. Nearly anyone says yes to more of something free. A question about their own week gives the board a number it can staff against.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ten questions is a sensible ceiling for a patron survey, with the decision question on the first screen. A student on a study break may stop at question four, and the answer to the first one still counts.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Leave names off when you can
fields.howto_step_5_des: With no name attached, a student can call the shelves dull without a second thought. For a reading or study space survey, ask Emergent to save no names, and say so on the first screen. Ask for a card number only when you need one answer per card.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Close two weeks before the vote
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close the survey two weeks before the board meeting that settles it. That leaves time to read every comment and write up the change. Put the open and close dates in your prompt, and Emergent builds them into the survey.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the result where patrons will see it, such as a sign at the desk or a line in the newsletter. A patron who sees that Sunday hours came from the survey has a reason to answer the next one.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a library survey that asks my 2,400 cardholders which hours they would use if the library opened on Sundays.

faq_plan.a: A library survey is a set of questions a library sends its patrons, students, or residents about how they use it and what should change, such as opening hours or the book collection. The name also covers the federal Public Libraries Survey, whose data are supplied annually by public libraries across the country.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a library survey?
faq_plan.a: Start with the decision the answers will settle, then draft questions a patron can finish on a phone. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the library, the people you want to hear from, and the decision, and Emergent builds the survey and the table that stores each response.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a library survey ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask how often the patron visits and what brings them in, then put the decision question near the top, such as which closed hours they would use. End with one open comment box. Keep every question about the patron's own use of the library rather than libraries in general.

faq_plan.q: What should a library survey for students ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask where students study and when they fail to find a seat, then ask what the library should carry for their courses. A single quiet rating per floor out of 5 is enough to compare floors. Keep it to a few questions, since students answer between classes.

faq_plan.q: Should a library survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Make it anonymous when the topic is personal, such as reading habits or how a student rates the staff. An anonymous survey cannot tell whether one person answered twice; a card number can. Emergent builds either version from a prompt, and a second prompt switches it.

faq_plan.q: Is a library user survey the same as the annual public library statistics report?
faq_plan.a: No. A user survey asks patrons what they want. The statistics report is filed by the library itself: the Kansas form, for example, includes questions about library visits, circulation, size of collections, public service hours, and staffing. Run a patron survey to learn why those numbers move.

faq_plan.q: How often should a library survey its patrons?
faq_plan.a: Run one general survey a year, at the same time each year so the results compare, and a short one before each decision that needs patron input, such as new hours. Space them out: the regulars who answer every time should not be asked twice in one month.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more patrons to answer a library survey?
faq_plan.a: Put the link where patrons already look, such as the checkout receipt or the email that says a hold is ready. Send one reminder a week after launch. Say on the first screen how long the survey takes and what it will decide.

faq_plan.q: How do I read library survey results?
faq_plan.a: Read the decision question first and count it by branch, since one busy branch can hide what a smaller one wants. Then read the comments for that question alone. Emergent builds the survey on a database the library owns, and the counts filter by branch or by date.

faq_plan.q: What should a library survey template include?
faq_plan.a: Include the decision question, two questions about how the patron uses the library, an open comment box, and a closing screen that says when results will be shared. On paid plans, Emergent exports the finished survey's code to your GitHub repository as next year's starting point.

plan.angle: The top 10 for library survey is government pages about the annual Public Libraries Survey that libraries file with their state, plus one how-to guide on user surveys and a strategic-planning guide. None shows a library building its own survey of patrons, students or residents and acting on the answers. This page is for that librarian: four library surveys built from a prompt and run to a decision (weekend hours at a public library, quiet seats at a college library, a middle school reading survey, a county needs survey for a strategic plan), a how-to on writing questions patrons finish, and an FAQ that separates the patron survey from the state statistics report.

Dellmont College library puts a QR code on every study table, 418 students rate quiet on each floor from their phones, the second floor averages 2.4 of 5, which emails the library dean, and the second floor becomes a silent floor for finals week.

The Tamsin Hill Middle School librarian asks students what they want to read with no names saved, 296 answer, 141 of 296 pick graphic novels, and $600 of the $1,200 spring book order goes to graphic novels.

Orrin County Library runs a community survey for its 2027 strategic plan through links at 5 branches and the county newsletter, 1,140 residents answer, laptop lending tops the Eastgate branch with 88 of 210, and the board writes laptop lending into the plan.
